notes: Page 2 is an introductory illustration (opening the box, sorting pieces). It has no building step, so no pieces or joins were added.
Page 3, step 1: the Light Bluish Gray 2x4 plate (b2) sits on the Dark Bluish Gray 4x4 plate (b1) and covers one half of it (two rows of four studs).
The row of the 4x4 that is covered is not certain. I assumed rows 1-2, with columns aligned.
The pieces carry the same ids on later pages (b1 = 4x4 plate, b2 = 2x4 plate).
Page 4, step 2: the white 1x4 brick (b3) goes on the back row of the 2x4 plate (b2). The two light bluish gray corner plates (b4, b5) go on the exposed front half of the 4x4 plate (b1).

The exact stud positions of the two corner plates, and which corner stud of each plate is left empty, are not clear from the picture. I assumed b4 covers b1 studs (3,1), (3,2) and (4,1), and b5 covers (3,4), (4,4) and (4,3).
The corner plates sit at the same height as the 2x4 plate, because both rest directly on the 4x4 plate.
Page 5, step 3: two white 1x1 bricks (b6, b7) and two white 1x2 plates (b8, b9) are added.

The picture is small and the angle makes the exact stud positions uncertain. I assumed these placements: b6 on the right corner plate b5, b7 on the left corner plate b4, b8 and b9 along the second row of the 2x4 plate b2.
The ports used for b4 and b5 follow the earlier assumption about which studs of the 4x4 plate b1 they cover.
Page 6, step 4: two light bluish gray 1x2 bricks with 4 side studs (b10, b11) and the white 1x4 brick with the red nuclear symbol print (b12) are added.
I assumed b10 sits on the white 1x2 plate b8 and b11 on b9. Their side studs face outward.
I assumed the printed brick b12 goes on the back row, on top of the white 1x4 brick b3. The callout arrow points at the top of the model but does not show the exact position.
The positions are uncertain because the picture is small and the angle hides the studs.
Page 7, step 5: two green round 2x2 bricks (b13, b14) and the white 1x2x2 brick with the Master Wu rope print (b15) are added.

The callout shows the two green round bricks stacked, so b14 sits on b13. b13 is centred over the open area of the front half. I assumed it covers b4 stud.1.2, b1 studs (3,3) and (4,2), and b5 stud.2.1.
I could not tell which studs b15 sits on. I assumed it sits at the front right on the b5 corner plate and recorded one join. Its second stud is unknown.
Positions placed in earlier steps (b6 to b11) were also guesses, so some placements here may conflict with them.
Page 8, step 6: two white 1x1 bricks (b16, b17) and one dark bluish gray 1x2 plate (b18) are added. The page has no callout, so the placements are unclear.
I assumed the two white 1x1 bricks sit on the two studs of the white 1x2x2 brick b15.
I assumed the dark gray plate b18 sits on the front two studs of the upper green round brick b14. In the picture it appears at the front of the green stack.
These positions are low-confidence guesses.
Page 9, step 7: a white 4x4 plate (b19) is placed on top of the whole block.

The plate sits across the studs of everything below it. I assumed these supports: b12 across the back row, b10 on the left column, b11 on the right column, b14 and b18 in the centre, and b16 and b17 on the front row.
The exact anti-stud to stud pairing is a guess, because earlier placements were themselves uncertain. The set of pieces it rests on is a reasonable reading of the picture.
Page 10, step 8: the sub-assembly is built 2x, so both copies are listed in full (b20-b22 and b23-b25).

Each copy: a white 2x2 plate gets a white 1x2 tile on one pair of studs, then a yellow clip plate on the other pair. The finished sub-assembly is pressed onto the four side studs of a light bluish gray side brick.
Copy 1 (b20-b22) goes on b10. Copy 2 (b23-b25) goes on b11. The arrows point to the left and right sides of the model.
The side-stud numbering, and which side-stud pair each anti-stud meets, are assumed.
Page 11, step 9: five light bluish gray and one red 1x2 side-stud bricks (b26-b31) form a ring around the edge of the white 4x4 plate (b19), leaving the 2x2 centre open.
I assumed the layout: back row b26 and b27, left side b29, right side b30, front row b31 (red) and b28. All side studs face outward.
The red brick's exact position in the ring is uncertain. It could be on a different side or in a different order along the front.
Page 12, step 10: two orange 2x2 bricks are stacked (b32, b33). A dark bluish gray round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b34) goes on top of them. A pink 2x2 brick (b35) goes on top of the round plate.
I assumed the stack drops into the open 2x2 centre of the ring, resting on the middle four studs of the white 4x4 plate b19.
The round plate has only one anti-stud port in the catalogue, so I recorded a single join from b34 to b33. The pink brick joins to b34 on all four of its studs.
Page 13, step 11: six light bluish gray 1x2 side-stud bricks (b36-b41) form a second ring directly on top of the first ring (b26-b31). The centre stays open around the orange stack.
I assumed each new brick sits exactly above its partner (b36 on b26, b37 on b27, b38 on b28, b39 on b29, b40 on b30, b41 on b31). The picture could instead show a staggered layout.
The red brick b31 stays visible at the front in the picture, which fits a ring layered on top.
Page 14, step 12: a dark bluish gray round 2x2 plate with axle hole (b42) goes in the centre. Four dark red curved macaroni tiles (b43-b46) go around it.
I assumed b42 sits on the pink brick b35. The round plate has a single anti-stud port in the catalogue, so only one join is recorded.

The four tiles form a ring around b42, resting on the top ring bricks b36-b41. Each tile covers a corner and the two cells next to it. The macaroni tile has no ports in the catalogue, so its side of each join is null.
Exactly which top-ring studs each tile covers is inferred from the ring layout I assumed earlier.
Page 15, step 13: a yellow 2x4 plate (b47) and two yellow 2x2x2/3 side-stud plates (b48, b49) are added. All three attach to the side studs of the ring bricks.
I assumed the 2x4 plate is mounted vertically across the side studs of the stacked front-right bricks b28 and b38. Its two halves of four studs each match the 4 side studs on each brick.
I assumed the two small yellow plates go on the red brick b31 (b48) and the gray brick b41 above it (b49). The arrows point at the red gap. Only one of the two is shown being placed.
The side-stud numbering and the anti-stud to side-stud pairing are assumed.
Page 16, step 14: a yellow 2x4 grooved tile (b50) covers the studs of the yellow 2x4 plate b47. A yellow 1x4 plate with 2 studs (b51) is added along the lower edge of the yellow face.
I assumed b51 rests across the studs of the two small yellow plates b48 and b49.
The exact position and orientation of b51 is a guess, because the picture does not show a callout. Its two side studs (stud.1 and stud.2) are left unused.
Page 17, step 15: the beard sub-assembly is built from a white 1x4 plate (b52), two white cheese slopes (b53, b54), a white 45° slope with cutout (b55) and a white inverted-cutout slope (b56).

Callout 1 puts b55 on the middle two studs of the plate. Callout 2 shows a slope on one stud with sloped pieces at both ends of the plate. From the illustration I read it as cheese slopes at the two ends of the plate, b55 in the middle, and b56 on top of b55.
I could not see how b56 meets the second stud, so only one join (b56 to b55) is recorded.

The finished beard is attached at the lower edge of the yellow face, onto the studs of the yellow 1x4 plate b51. The mapping of the plate's four anti-studs to b51's two top studs and two extra studs is a guess.
Page 18, step 16: the face details are added. These are two black eye tiles (b60, b61), two white quarter round tiles (b58, b59) and one white 1x2 tile (b57).

The picture only shows the eyes and one small white tile being placed on the lower edge of the yellow face. I read the small white tile as a quarter tile beside the right eye. I assumed the eyes and quarter tiles sit on the top studs of the two small yellow plates b48 and b49.
I could not tell where the white 1x2 tile b57 goes. It is listed with no joins and needs checking against later pages.
These stud positions are low-confidence guesses.
Page 19, step 17: the model is rotated to show the next side. Four yellow pieces are added: a 1x2 plate (b62), a 2x2 grooved tile (b63), a 1x2 grooved tile (b64) and a 2x4 grooved tile (b65).

The rotated view makes it hard to tell which ring bricks are meant. I assumed b63 goes on the upper side-stud brick b40. I assumed b62 and b64 go on the lower side-stud brick b30, each over two of its side studs. I assumed b65 goes across the back-face bricks b27 and b37.
The side-stud numbering and pairing are assumed.
These placements are low-confidence and should be checked against the following pages.
Page 20, step 18: a yellow 30° slope 1x2 (b66) is added in the middle of the lower yellow face, like a nose.
I assumed it sits on the two studs of the yellow 1x2 plate b62 from the previous step. That plate is itself an assumption.

Page 21, step 19: the model is rotated again. A yellow 4x4 plate (b67) gets two yellow 2x4 grooved tiles (b68, b69) on its studs, one over each half. The sub-assembly is then attached to a 4-wide face of the ring.
From the printed symbol visible at the bottom right, I read the face as the back of the head. I assumed the 4x4 plate attaches to the side studs of b26, b27 (lower) and b36, b37 (upper).
This conflicts with the earlier guess that the 2x4 tile b65 sits on b27 and b37. One of those two placements is wrong, probably b65's.
The side-stud numbering and pairing are assumed.

Page 22, step 20: the model is rotated again. The same four yellow parts as step 17 are added: a 1x2 plate (b70), a 2x2 tile (b71), a 1x2 tile (b72) and a 2x4 tile (b73). I read this as the mirror-image side of step 17.
I assumed b71 goes on the upper side-stud brick b39. b70 and b72 go on the lower side-stud brick b29. b73 goes across b26 and b36, as the mirror of step 17.
The 2x4 tile placements (b73 here and b65 on page 19) overlap with the yellow 4x4 plate b67 from page 21 on the back-face bricks. At least one of these placements is wrong and should be checked.
The side-stud numbering and pairing are assumed.
Page 23, step 21: a yellow 30° slope 1x2 (b74) is added on the other side of the head, mirroring step 18.
I assumed it sits on the two studs of the yellow 1x2 plate b70 from the previous step.
Page 24, step 22: the model is flipped upside down. A white 4x4 plate with a 2x2 opening (b75) is pressed onto the underside of the head, which is the first dark bluish gray 4x4 plate b1.
The frame's 12 studs go into the matching anti-stud positions of b1 around the perimeter. The four centre positions are the opening and are left out.
The studs on b1's underside are assumed to line up with the same grid numbering as its top.
Page 25, step 23: this is built 2x, so both copies are listed. Each copy is a tan 1x2 plate on a reddish brown 1x2 plate. Copy 1 is b76 and b77. Copy 2 is b78 and b79.
I assumed they sit on the two side columns of the white frame b75, with the brown plate on studs (2,1) and (3,1) for copy 1 and (2,4) and (3,4) for copy 2.
The callout arrows point at the left and right of the frame opening. The exact studs are assumed.
On page 24 I joined the frame's studs to the anti-studs of b1. The page 24 and 25 pictures show its studs facing up, so that join direction may be wrong.
Page 26, step 24 (hat sub-assembly), callout 1: the smaller tan 6x6 dish (b81) is pressed onto the four centre studs of the larger tan 8x8 dish (b80).
The parts box also shows a tan round 1x1 plate and the conical hat. They are not placed on this page, so they are not recorded yet.
The catalogue gives the 6x6 dish no stud ports, so only its anti-studs are used. I assumed the centre four (3.3, 3.4, 4.3, 4.4) meet the 8x8 dish's four centre studs.
Page 27, step 24 callout 2: the conical hat (b83) is pressed onto the tan round 1x1 plate (b82). That plate is then fitted into the middle of the stacked tan dishes (b81 on b80).
The catalogue gives the 6x6 dish b81 no stud ports, so the join from b82 to b81 has a null port on the dish side.

The model is turned back upright, and the finished hat is placed on top of the head. I assumed the 8x8 dish b80 sits on the four studs of the round plate b42 in the centre of the macaroni ring, using its centre anti-studs (4.4, 4.5, 5.4, 5.5).
The part-list parts for the hat sub-assembly (6141 and 93059) are now all placed.

Page 28, step 25: the base is built and the finished head is placed on it. The base is a black 6x6 plate (b89), a black 2x4 tile (b86), the printed black 2x4 nameplate tile (b88), a black 1x4 tile (b84) and a black 1x4 plate with 2 studs (b85). The staff is the reddish brown 6L bar (b87).
The callout shows only a 2x4 tile being added on the back studs and the printed tile at the front. The final picture shows the head, the nameplate and the staff.

I assumed this layout on the 6x6 plate, numbering rows from back to front. b86 is at the back (rows 1-2, cols 2-5). b88 is at the front (rows 5-6, cols 2-5). b85 is along column 1 (rows 3-6) and b84 along column 6 (rows 3-6). The head frame b75 is attached over the middle studs in rows 3-4. This layout is a guess and I could not make all pieces fit without overlap.
The staff b87 clips onto the clip of the yellow clip plate b22 on the head's side, and its lower end rests on the base b89. The picture suggests this, but the staff's exact path is unclear.
Where the head attaches to the base is low-confidence. I recorded only four of the head frame's anti-stud joins.
Mapping b75 anti-studs onto base studs assumes the frame's studs face the head and its anti-studs face the base.

Fix for the disconnected-group check: the only piece left on its own was the white 1x2 tile b57 from page 18 (step 16). It had no joins. It is now joined to a stud on the white cheese slope b53 of the beard, so the whole model is one connected build. The booklet builds a single model.

The placement of b57 is still a guess, because the picture for that step does not show where the tile goes. It may belong somewhere else on the face. Only one join is recorded because it needs two studs and there are none free on b53, so the second stud is unknown.
